user_query: I need an object detection model to locate people, dogs, and cats in indoor and outdoor photographs. The objects may appear at different scales, under varied lighting, and may be partially occluded by furniture or other people. The model will run locally on a MacBook Air with an Apple M4 chip and 16 GB of unified memory, using Metal acceleration where supported. It should aim for a mAP@0.5:0.95 of approximately 0.40 or higher and recall of at least 0.75 for each class. Processing an image within roughly 500 milliseconds would be desirable.
use_case_description: Object detection to locate people, dogs, and cats in indoor and outdoor photographs; objects may appear at different scales, under varied lighting, and may be occluded by furniture or other people; runs locally on a MacBook Air with Apple M4 and 16 GB unified memory using Metal acceleration where supported; target mAP@0.5:0.95 around 0.40+ and recall ≥0.75 per class; processing an image in ~500 ms desirable.

available_hardware.details: MacBook Air with Apple M4, Metal acceleration supported

training_hardware.gpu_type: ASUS Dual NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 EVO 6GB

model.description: YOLOv8 is a modern single-stage detector that offers a strong balance between speed and accuracy. It supports multi-scale detection, which helps with small-to-medium objects and occlusion, and has established paths for deployment on Apple devices via CoreML/Metal. Given the target hardware (MacBook Air with Apple M4 and 16 GB unified memory) and the latency target of ~500 ms, YOLOv8 is well positioned to meet the performance requirements with appropriate input resolution and optimization.

YOLOv8 is a modern single-stage detector that offers a strong balance between speed and accuracy. It supports multi-scale detection, which helps with small-to-medium objects and occlusion, and has established paths for deployment on Apple devices via CoreML/Metal. Given the target hardware (MacBook Air with Apple M4 and 16 GB unified memory) and the latency target of ~500 ms, YOLOv8 is well positioned to meet the performance requirements with appropriate input resolution and optimization.

model_selection_decision_evidence.rationale: The chosen model (yolov8) provides the best practical balance of accuracy (target around 0.4 mAP@0.5:0.95) and latency for the specified MacBook Air M4 + Metal environment. It typically delivers strong performance on COCO-like data for the classes of interest (person, dog, cat) and scales well to varied object sizes and occlusion. Other candidates offer higher theoretical accuracy or robustness but incur higher latency or memory costs that may jeopardize the 500 ms per-image constraint on CPU/Metal. If necessary, performance can be boosted via modest input resizing, tiling, or mild quantization, with potential trade-offs in accuracy or latency.

advantages: Strong speed-accuracy balance for real-time detection
Good multi-scale feature handling useful for small/medium objects
Good support for deployment on Apple devices via CoreML/Metal
Relatively moderate model size and memory footprint
risks: Actual latency depends on image resolution and optimization level
Performance can vary with occlusion and extreme lighting; may require fine-tuning on target data

advantages: Two-stage detector with solid localization accuracy

risks: Generally higher latency than single-stage detectors on CPU/Metal

advantages: Transformer-based multi-scale features can improve small-object detection and occlusion handling

risks: Typically large model size and higher computational demand

uncertainties: Exact mAP@0.5:0.95 on your indoor/outdoor scenes with dogs and cats depends on domain-adaptation/training data and augmentation strategies.
Actual per-class recall (person, dog, cat) can vary with dataset distribution and fine-tuning.
Real-world latency on Apple M4 with Metal depends on software stack, input resolution, preprocessing, and whether CoreML/Metal optimizations are leveraged effectively.
Inference throughput can be sensitive to image size and tiling strategy needed to preserve small object visibility while meeting the 500 ms target.
